extracted.intended_audience: U.S. Congress, federal policymakers, and scientific administrators planning national research policy
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and recommended criteria for creating and operating a U.S. National Research Foundation, including its organization, powers, funding, international activities, library and information services, patent policy, and relationships with universities, industry, and the military.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support and sponsorship of international cooperative scientific enterprises
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommend that the National Research Foundation be charged with the responsibility of participating in such international cooperative scientific enterprises as it deems desirable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Government could provide modest financing and facilitate travel, visas, and official courtesies; example: International Polar Year pooled methods and data to add value. Foundation participation is recommended to promote official methods of carrying on international scientific activity.

rubrics_metrics.name: International scientific congresses
rubrics_metrics.description: The Foundation should participate in arrangements for international scientific conferences whereby scientific workers in different countries may be brought together to exchange ideas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such conferences were stimulating and useful prewar; the Foundation can help with government financial aid, official courtesies, travel arrangements, and recognition for foreign visitors, especially where U.S. representatives have been hampered by lack of government support.

rubrics_metrics.name: International fellowships
rubrics_metrics.description: The Foundation should be empowered to grant scholarships and fellowships to qualified scientists, awarding some to Americans for foreign travel and study and to scientists from abroad to undertake advanced research in the U.S.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Program promotes scientific progress and international understanding; holders are likely disinterested representatives; should be undertaken with care to avoid specialized political or personal interests and should draw on National Research Council and private foundation experience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific attachés
rubrics_metrics.description: As an experiment, scientific attachés should be appointed to serve in certain selected U.S. embassies; they should be men of high professional scientific attainments with temporary tenure (perhaps 1 or 2 years).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Principal duties: facilitate aspects of scientific cooperation, improve knowledge of science abroad and contribute U.S. experience. Especially important in countries (e.g., Russia) where scientific activity is government-controlled and other channels restricted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Function of the National Research Foundation
rubrics_metrics.description: The Foundation's function should be to assist and encourage research in the public interest by disbursement of funds allocated by Congress.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Its board of trustees should be eminent men cognizant of science needs and experienced in administration; members appointed by the President from a panel nominated by the National Academy of Sciences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capitalization and multi-year budgeting
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed original nonearning capitalization of $500,000,000 to be called and expended, with the approval of Congress, over not less than 10 years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scientists emphasize importance of a board that (1) can budget over a considerable period, (2) will not be subject to detailed legislative review, and (3) will be able to withstand political pressures; but the Foundation must remain accountable to President, Congress, and public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board independence balanced with accountability
rubrics_metrics.description: Board should have sufficient freedom to budget and act without detailed legislative micromanagement while remaining accountable to President, Congress, and the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid instruments that would insulate the Foundation entirely from oversight, but also avoid hampering limitations that lead to inflexibility and inefficiency; examples of desirable features cited (British University Grants Committee).

rubrics_metrics.name: Board composition, terms, and remuneration
rubrics_metrics.description: Board of trustees should comprise about 15 members, serving part-time, with remuneration at $50 per diem when on official duty plus travel and subsistence; normal term ~5 years with no reappointment until 2 years lapse and staggered terms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Staggering ensures continuity; initial appointments should vary in length; aim to maintain age distribution to assure dynamic leadership.

rubrics_metrics.name: Executive director and professional executive staff
rubrics_metrics.description: Board should have the power to appoint an executive director of recognized ability as a full-time officer with commensurate salary; executive staff of experts should be full-time professional employees responsible for major science divisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Staff experts (physical sciences, biological sciences, engineering, agriculture, etc.) keep in touch with research nationwide, lighten board administrative burden, and enable board to focus on policy decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain close contact with research nationally
rubrics_metrics.description: The Foundation must confront the problem of maintaining close contact with research in all parts of the country.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Executive staff and regional contacts are expected to monitor research activity nationally to inform policy and funding decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Power (a): Study and keep informed on state of science
rubrics_metrics.description: To study and keep itself currently informed on the present state of science in the United States and to seek ways of applying its resources to the discovery of useful knowledge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ongoing assessment of national scientific status to guide resource allocation and program priorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Power (b): Initiate, encourage, sponsor and finance research with stated emphases
rubrics_metrics.description: To initiate, encourage, sponsor and finance scientific research and development with emphasis on (1) increasing the general fund of basic scientific knowledge and thus creating new industries and increased employment, (2) promoting the conservation and better utilization of natural resources, and (3) improving the health of the Nation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Utilize existing federal, state, educational, foundation, laboratory, and institute facilities to the greatest extent feasible. No contract or grant-in-aid should introduce Foundation control over internal policies or operations of the contractor or grantee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Power (c): Establish or provide new research facilities (but not operate them)
rubrics_metrics.description: To establish or provide new or additional scientific and technical research facilities in geographical areas or specialized fields where none exist or existing facilities are inadequate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provided that the Foundation should not itself undertake directly to operate such facilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Power (d): Collection and dissemination of scientific knowledge
rubrics_metrics.description: To provide for and assure the most comprehensive collection and dissemination of scientific and technical knowledge and information by aids to libraries, bibliographic services, translating activities, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support for library aids and information infrastructure is an explicit Foundation responsibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Power (e): Seek latent talent and support education/training
rubrics_metrics.description: To seek out latent scientific talent, and to foster and support scientific and technical education and training through grants to individuals, educational institutions, foundations, laboratories and institutes, and through scholarships, fellowships and prizes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Active talent-spotting and support mechanisms to build research workforce and capacity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Power (f): Afford opportunities to scientists, inventors, research workers
rubrics_metrics.description: To assist scientists, inventors, and research workers by affording them opportunities to engage in research and developmental activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide practical support and access to research opportunities as a core function.

rubrics_metrics.name: Power (g): Advise government in cooperation with National Academy of Sciences
rubrics_metrics.description: To act in cooperation with the National Academy of Sciences in advising the President, the Congress, and the various departments, independent establishments, and agencies of the Government on scientific matters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formal advisory role coordinating with NAS to inform national science policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Power (h): Make resources available in war or national emergency
rubrics_metrics.description: To make its facilities, personnel and resources fully available to the United States in the event of war or the declaration of a national emergency by the President or the Congress.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Foundation operations should be adaptable to national emergency needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Power (i): Cooperate with military research organizations and coordinate to avoid duplication
rubrics_metrics.description: To cooperate with the Army, Navy, and civilian military research organizations for the rapid interchange of information on basic scientific problems of use in national defense, and to coordinate activities wherever possible to prevent unnecessary duplication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coordinate basic-science information flow with defense organizations while preventing redundant effort.

rubrics_metrics.name: Power (j): Assist industry and small enterprises to apply discoveries
rubrics_metrics.description: To assist industry and business, particularly small enterprises, in establishing research facilities and in obtaining scientific and technical information and guidance to expedite the transition from scientific discovery to technological application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support for technology transfer and assistance to small business is an explicit Foundation role.

rubrics_metrics.name: Power (k): Counter-cyclical grant-making in depression periods
rubrics_metrics.description: To help maintain a continuous and steady expansion of scientific research by increasing its grants for research in periods of depression, as far as is consistent with sound and equitable policy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use grant-making to stabilize research activity during economic downturns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Power (l): Represent U.S. in international scientific cooperation and exchanges
rubrics_metrics.description: To represent the United States in effecting better international cooperation in scientific activities, to assist in the freer international exchange of scientific and technical knowledge and information and scientific and technical personnel, and to help sponsor and finance international scientific congresses or associations and cooperative scientific research programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Active international representation, sponsorship, and facilitation of personnel exchanges are recommended Foundation functions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grants for historical and economic studies
rubrics_metrics.description: The board should be empowered to make grants for such historical and economic studies as it believes necessary to fulfill its responsibilities in investigating scientific research and its practical applications in industry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support for analysis of research and application history/economics to inform policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reliance on character and qualifications of board members
rubrics_metrics.description: Confidence must be reposed in the integrity, character, and qualifications of individuals comprising the board; no curbs or limitations can substitute for character and ability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid a series of hampering limitations on board powers which would lead to inflexibility and inefficient operation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent policy: minimal interference with university practices
rubrics_metrics.description: The Foundation should set up its own general rules for the handling of patent policies and should interfere as little as possible with the practices of the different universities and research institutions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Obtaining patents by universities on Foundation-financed work expected to remain a minor byproduct; university patent policies should not interfere with early publication of results; recipients' patent policies should foster widespread public use of worthwhile developments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Library aids: three-pronged information services approach
rubrics_metrics.description: Adequate technical libraries are indispensable; services to be considered under (A) interlibrary cooperation, (B) abstracting and translating services, and (C) bibliographic and reference services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Federal attention and part of Foundation funds should be devoted to these large-scale, centralized problems which private resources cannot fully address.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interlibrary cooperation — securing and distributing copies; union catalogues
rubrics_metrics.description: Secure at least one copy of all needed items and an appropriate distribution of copies so that titles are strategically available; participating institutions can maintain 'working libraries' and rely on cooperative holdings for the rest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cooperation may take the form of agreements to be inclusive in limited fields, union catalogues regionally and nationally, and organized transportation arrangements; strengthen Library of Congress and similar institutions to foster cooperation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reproduction of scarce or wartime-lost foreign publications
rubrics_metrics.description: Government should provide funds to reproduce much European wartime-restricted or destroyed material so American libraries do not show serious gaps in foreign periodical literature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reproducing this material is beyond private resources and is a federal concern.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstracting services require stable funding
rubrics_metrics.description: Abstracting publications are laborious and expensive (reading, summarizing, editing, printing); many are supported by donated scientist time and face financial deficits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If unpaid contributions cannot continue, substantial costs will be incurred and government or Foundation support should be considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Translating services: need and cost, especially for Russian literature
rubrics_metrics.description: With Russia as an important contributor to science, translating services (e.g., of Russian works) become acute and expensive; government should consider methods to meet costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Translation benefits U.S. science and may promote English usage abroad; specific studies (e.g., biology) are underway to estimate costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bibliographic and reference services: indices, reference access, and technological aids
rubrics_metrics.description: Consolidated cumulative indices are lacking in many fields; reference services often restricted to established workers; use of business machines and microfilm might improve searching and bibliography production.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider reclassifying past literature and arranging for classification of every article prior to publication; improve services so younger researchers can access past work without undue diversion from research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research funding adequacy metric: direct operating expense per dollar of professional salary
rubrics_metrics.description: Comparison metric: industrial labs and institutes show direct operating expenses typically near $1 per $1 of professional salary (min ~ $0.40), while university departments typically about $0.20 per $1 (often lower).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Higher ratios in industry correlate with greater research productivity; universities with low ratios likely have many researchers whose productivity could be raised by providing more research funds (equipment, technical assistance, reduced teaching loads).

rubrics_metrics.name: Encouraging research in small colleges
rubrics_metrics.description: Small colleges can encourage research by grants-in-aid from special funds, leaves of absence for faculty, maintaining machine/shops for department use, and liberal purchase policies for instruments usable in teaching and research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These policies can produce well-equipped labs and provide valuable wartime/peacetime research contributions; many small liberal-arts colleges could contribute if funds were available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respect concerns about federal subsidy and political control
rubrics_metrics.description: Some nonresearch institutions oppose federal subsidy fearing political control, which they view as harmful based on totalitarian examples; others believe funds would enable modest research activity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In designing a federal aid program, attention should be given to avoiding political control while enabling potential contributors among small colleges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data and estimation caveats for research-expenditure analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Research-expenditure data were collected by questionnaire with varying accounting systems; estimates and postwar needs are rough approximations (e.g., $26,000,000 prewar to $57,000,000 postwar estimates for ~150 research universities).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy decisions should recognize limitations of the data and that many universities provided lists of projects ready to undertake if funds and personnel were available.
